pr.title: feat(local): route approved merge trains through the daemon
pr.body:
### Motivation
- Address #593. The reviewed merge-train tool needs a daemon caller so independently approved stale PRs can be integrated while model lanes remain disabled.

### Description
- Match a requested batch's pinned heads against the approved-candidate scan and preserve the PR-to-SHA mapping into the train. Compare pins under member claims and retain checks for accepted and dropped members in the publication verifier.
- Prepare the primary checkout without discarding local history. Require every unpublished commit's paths and modes to satisfy the existing passive-telemetry policy before synchronization.
- Invoke the existing train synchronously, preserving its combined CI, claims, leases and post-push checks. Keep the individual-PR path and number-only standalone train callers, and provide a concrete deployment patch and activation instructions.
- Runtime activation and the first live batch remain downstream of independent review and merge.

### Testing
- Published head `c55a406975d6b17ec4a92f993fc6d76105439d42`: all nine local CI statuses passed in 383 seconds. All eight gates ran, including build, blueprint rendering, synchronization and statement-origin.
- The CI suite and normal commit hook each passed 741 tests with 9 skipped. Nine focused adapter tests, eight selected train scenarios and the dropped-pin verifier regression also passed, covering the two reported failure paths and unchanged callers/conflict drops.
- The rooted axiom audit passed 1,659 declarations with zero failures and three existing statement-level warnings. No proof-level leanok declaration depends on sorryAx.
- The worktree is clean and fifteen repair-handoff artifact hashes were verified. The deployment patch and active runtime hashes remain unchanged; no daemon activation or live train has run.
- A fresh bounded F1/F2/integration recheck of review 5244965776 remains required.

---
Addresses #593

# Review - PR 595 @ c55a406975d6b17ec4a92f993fc6d76105439d42

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: 2e25304971b70661bc990bbcddefbcde6edd0bd6. Bounded recheck of the two findings of review 5244965776 and their integration, over a 608-line, 9-file Python/protocol/deployment change (no Lean touched), against base `main` at merge-base b6c09eb0.

## Findings

- none

## Review

Scope of this pass, as instructed by the main session: only the repair of the two findings of review 5244965776 (recorded at previous head 00e2079f) and whether it weakens anything that review accepted. The complete first review was not redone and the 507/579/592 transport contract was not reopened.

F1 (approved head pins lost on handoff) - repaired. `local/bin/daemon_train.py:107-110` now expands the scan-time pins into `--pinned-head <pr> <sha>` arguments alongside the numbers. `local/bin/pr_train.py:419` parses them, `run_train` (pr_train.py:319-322) requires the pin set to name every member with a full 40-hex SHA, and the comparison happens inside `members_at` (pr_train.py:100-103) - i.e. after `member_claims` and the per-PR file locks are already held (pr_train.py:328-337), which is exactly the scan-to-claim window the first finding named. A mismatch raises `GateFailure`, which `members_at` aggregates and re-raises, so the whole train refuses rather than transporting an unpinned head. The pins are carried into the manifest (`requested_heads`, pr_train.py:353-354) and re-checked by `verify_manifest` after combined CI and before the push, including conflict-dropped members (pr_train.py:183-199). Tests cover it: `test_pinned_train_refuses_a_new_independently_green_head` (a replacement head with its own green CI and approval still refuses, remote main unchanged, claims released), `test_verifier_refuses_green_replacement_for_dropped_pin`, `test_pinned_train_keeps_pins_while_dropping_a_conflict`, and `test_train_failure_is_not_described_as_a_merge` asserts the exact argv the adapter hands to the train. `test_head_change_or_adjudication_refuses_batch` keeps the scan-side check.

F2 (net-tree base predicate) - repaired. `daemon_train.py:69-77` replaces the single `github/main..main` tree comparison with `unpublished_history_is_telemetry`, which walks `rev-list --reverse remote..local` and applies the existing `pr_merge._base_advance_is_tolerated` to every parent-to-commit step; a missing parent (root commit) or any failing git call fails closed, and a merge commit is checked against all its parents. Reuse of the established path-and-mode policy rather than a second predicate is the right call here. Tests: `test_reverted_nontelemetry_commits_never_reach_sync` (change then exact revert, net diff empty, still refused and `github-sync.sh` never invoked) and `test_reverted_telemetry_executable_mode_never_reaches_sync` (mode flip then restore). `test_preparation_retains_local_telemetry_and_uses_existing_sync` still shows legitimate telemetry-only leads being published by the existing sync, not reset or rebased.

Integration: nothing the first review accepted is weakened. `member_claims` still covers every member for the whole transport and re-verification; the pin logic is purely additive and gated on `expected_heads is not None`, so number-only standalone trains behave as before (`test_pinned_train_refuses_a_new_independently_green_head` ends by running the unpinned train successfully). `verify_manifest` validates the shape of `requested_heads` before trusting it and requires it to cover members plus drops exactly. `prepare_primary` keeps the ordering check-then-sync-then-`primary_at`, so the ancestry test precedes any publication. The deployment patch stays consistent with the adapter's CLI (`--repo-root`, `--batch-file`, candidate scan on stdin), adds a hard PAR=0 refusal, keeps the individual merge path, and leaves publication ownership with `pr_train.py`/`checked-push.sh` (no force-push, no new server predicate). Protocol prose in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md` and `EVOLUTION.md` and the `results/telemetry/events.md` bullet describe the implemented behaviour accurately, including that a changed pin refuses even with a green reviewed replacement and that reversed nontelemetry history requires operator reconciliation; no prose claims more than the code does.

Verification run: `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_daemon_train.py'` in the PR worktree at this head - 9 tests, OK; `scripts.tests.test_pr_train` - 31 tests including the three new pin tests, all passing (the only error in my first invocation was my own dotted-module call without `local/bin` on `sys.path`, not a defect: CI's `ci.sh:958` discovery run is green). Exact-head status: all nine `local-ci/*` contexts success; `local-review/summary` is failure only from the aborted earlier recheck, for the main session to republish.

Not checked: no Lean or blueprint file is touched, so the faithfulness and proof-integrity ladder is not applicable beyond confirming the diff adds no `sorry`/`axiom`/`native_decide` and no statement change; the live daemon runtime script was not inspected or run, and no train was executed. The recorded runtime hashes in the deployment note are unverifiable from the repository and remain an operator precondition. The append-only conflict on `results/telemetry/events.md` is not a finding, per the merge tool's both-sides record policy.

One non-blocking observation, deliberately not raised as a finding: `verify_manifest` re-runs the full gate for conflict-dropped members, so an unrelated late gate change on a dropped PR would refuse an otherwise good publication. That is fail-closed and consistent with the transport contract.

VERDICT: APPROVED (code=APPROVED, prose=APPROVED)
